debate.name: Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd

rounds.text: Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd is demonstrating exceptional top-line and bottom-line expansion, evidenced by a 5-year compounded sales growth of 41% [E14], a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 50% [E16], and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 57% [E17]. This strong operational momentum is backed by healthy cash generation, with a cash conversion ratio of 1.21x and operating cash flow reaching Rs 205 Cr for March 2026 [E30, E31]. The company's growth strategy is actively funded by substantial capital investments, as reflected in capital work-in-progress rising by 137.3% to Rs 242 Cr in September 2026 [E36], while maintaining a conservative balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.25x [E33] and a comfortable current ratio of 3.87x [E34]. Institutional investors have recognized this trajectory, resulting in positive money flow [E40], foreign institutional holdings increasing to 7.05% [E38], and domestic institutional holdings rising to 10.94% [E39] from December 2023 levels. Furthermore, the stock displays tremendous relative strength with a rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E47], trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E46], and benefiting from a supportive healthcare sector tailwind score of +0.69 [E70]. Conceded: [E1] and [E41], the stock trades at a rich P/E of 53.4 [E1] with a DCF-based intrinsic value calculation leaving a negative margin of safety [E41, E42].

The valuation of Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd rests on expectations that the underlying financials do not support [E67]. The stock trades at an expensive P/E of 53.4x and an EV/EBITDA of 27.68x, both of which command substantial premiums over sector benchmarks [E1, E11]. A discounted cash flow model values the intrinsic worth at Rs 770 per share against a market price of Rs 1,056, resulting in an unjustified negative margin of safety of -37.2% [E41, E42]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF reveals that the current market price already bakes in an unrealistic 22.4% earnings growth rate, surpassing the base case projection of 18.0% [E43]. Margin compression adds fundamental pressure, with the TTM operating margin falling to 23% from 29% three years prior, continuing a four-year downward trend [E26, E28]. Balance sheet risks are also mounting as borrowings have surged to Rs 468 Cr from Rs 264 Cr a year earlier, accompanied by a negative free cash flow of Rs -112 Cr and warning flags regarding potential interest capitalization [E32, E35, E59]. Finally, insiders have been reducing their exposure, with promoter holdings sliding by 10.64 percentage points since December 2023 [E37]. Conceded: compounding sales growth over the trailing twelve months is robust at 50%, alongside a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.25x [E16, E33].

Conceded: the intrinsic value from the discounted cash flow sits at Rs 770 against the market price of Rs 1,056 [E41]. However, the bear ignores that the rules-based screen explicitly rates the company an 85 out of 100 on fundamental strength, driven by massive top-line acceleration [E61, E62]. While valuations look rich, the company commands sector-beating returns on assets of 7.01% compared to the 6.3% benchmark [E8], and operates within a robust healthcare sector tailwind score of +0.69 [E70]. The surge in borrowings to Rs 468 Cr [E35] funds a massive 137.3% expansion in capital-work-in-progress [E36], directly fueling the exceptional 50% trailing twelve-month sales growth [E16]. Furthermore, institutional investors recognize this immense growth potential, driving positive money flow with a 1.53 percentage point increase in holdings [E40], backed by strong foreign and domestic institutional participation [E38, E39]. Finally, cash conversion remains pristine at 1.21x with Rs 205 Cr in operating cash flow for March 2026, proving that reported profits are fully backed by cash [E30, E31].

Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 205 Cr with a cash conversion ratio of 1.21x in March 2026 [E30, E31], but the bull relies on a low-confidence 85/100 screen score [E61] that explicitly flags a -37.2% margin of safety against an intrinsic DCF value of Rs 770 [E41, E42, E66]. This steep valuation disconnect is reinforced by a P/E of 56.16x against the sector benchmark of 30.87x [E6], a P/B of 5.44x against 2.88x [E7], an EV/EBITDA of 27.68x against 16.27x [E11], and a reverse DCF demanding 22.4% earnings growth compared to the 18.0% base case [E43]. Furthermore, while the bull highlights a 7.01% ROA [E8], it ignores that ROCE of 10.79% trails the 11.68% sector benchmark [E10], ROE of 10.16% trails the 10.53% sector benchmark [E9], and return on equity has decayed from a 5-year median of 14% down to 10% last year [E23, E25, E58]. Moreover, the expansion in CWIP [E36] and borrowings of Rs 468 Cr [E35] has driven free cash flow into negative territory at Rs -112 Cr [E32], even as operating margins dropped 6 percentage points from 29% to 23% over a 4-year decreasing trend [E26, E28] alongside potential interest cost capitalization [E59]. Finally, while institutional money flow is positive [E40], promoters have steadily dumped equity, reducing their stake by 10.64 percentage points down to 55.80% [E37, E60] as recent price growth outpaces profit delivery by 7% [E53].

Conceded: intrinsic value sits at Rs 770 per share in the DCF [E41, E42, E66], and promoter holdings have decreased by 10.64 percentage points [E37, E60]. However, the rules-based screen scores an 85 out of 100 on the back of explosive momentum, with sales surging 54% year-over-year and quarterly net profit rising 17% year-over-year [E61, E62, E64]. The premium multiples cited are fully justified by elite growth metrics, including a 5-year compounded sales growth of 41% and a stellar 57% compounded profit growth over the same period, vastly outperforming sector medians of 19.3% and 15.6% respectively [E6, E7, E11, E14, E17, E71, E72]. Furthermore, operating cash flow reached Rs 205 Cr with a strong 1.21x cash conversion backing reported profits [E30, E31], while working capital requirements meaningfully improved from 101 days down to 80.1 days [E57]. Institutional money flow remains positive as foreign and domestic institutions actively increase their stakes [E38, E39, E40], and the company operates under a supportive healthcare sector tailwind score of +0.69 [E68, E70] alongside a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E47].

Conceded: sales growth over 5 years is 41% [E14], compounded profit growth over 5 years is 57% [E17], working capital requirements reduced from 101 days to 80.1 days [E57], and institutional money flow is positive with foreign and domestic holdings increasing [E38, E39, E40]. However, citing an 85 out of 100 rules-based screen rating ignores that this specific score explicitly comes with a low confidence flag [E61]. The heavy reliance on historical sales and profit growth ignores that operating margins have been decreasing over the last four years, dropping from 29% to 23% in the trailing twelve months [E26, E28]. While operating cash flow reached Rs 205 Cr [E31], free cash flow landed deep in the negative at Rs -112 Cr [E32], undermining the durability of those earnings. Borrowings have simultaneously climbed to Rs 468 Cr from Rs 264 Cr a year earlier [E35], while filed statements explicitly flag a negative risk that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E59]. Finally, price growth exceeding profit growth by 7% indicates that expectations are running ahead of delivery [E53], leaving the valuation vulnerable despite the sector tailwind score of +0.69 [E68, E70].
